files.title: Context file
files.body:
# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act V VERIFY · Scale: Solo / small. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
VERIFY is part of the **Delivery track** — Are we building the thing right? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## VERIFY: Demonstrate with evidence that the increment works as specified, meets its quality attributes and solves the right problem — at a risk someone has knowingly accepted.
- **5.1 Test Strategy & Planning** — gate: Test Plan Approved. Produces: Quality risk analysis, Test strategy, Release test plan, Test environment record, Test data plan.
- **5.2 Functional Verification** — gate: Verification Signed. Produces: Test cases traced to criteria, Traceability matrix, Test-run evidence, Exploratory session sheet, Regression suite, Verification sign-off.
- **5.3 Non-Functional Verification** — gate: NFR Verification. Produces: Performance test report, Security test report, Accessibility audit report, Resilience test report, Non-functional results, Extraction accuracy evaluation.
- **5.4 Acceptance & Validation** — gate: Acceptance Sign-off. Produces: UAT plan, UAT execution log, Outcome validation report, UAT sign-off.
- **5.5 Defect Triage & Resolution** — gate: Quality Gate. Produces: Defect log, Defect & residual-risk report, Risk acceptances, Quality gate record, Verification retrospective, Learning log.
- Act gate: **Quality Gate** — decided by: QA lead decides the gate with the product owner; the business acceptor signs UAT; the risk owner accepts residual risk; the sponsor rules above appetite..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: STY → TST → TC → TR → NFT → UAT → DEF → RRA → QGR → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `verify-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Solo / small
I play all the roles. Keep every output short (one page or one screen), merge steps where it makes sense, and skip formal sign-offs — but keep the decision record and the learning log.
Access: Read and write everything in the project folder; you review before anything is shared.

files.title: Accessibility reviewer
files.body:
---
name: accessibility-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Accessibility lens — Usable by people with disabilities; WCAG. Use after: 5.1.1.1 S2 Identify quality risks; 5.1.2.1 S2 Choose levels, types & techniques per risk; 5.3.3.1 S1 Scan screens automatically; 5.3.3.1 S2 Walk through by keyboard."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Accessibility reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at access for people with disabilities: conformance with WCAG and support for assistive technologies.

## Questions to ask
- Can people with disabilities use it?
- Did research include them?
- Which accessibility standard applies?

## Concerns to check
- Excluding users
- Legal exposure

## Evidence this lens needs
- Inclusive research sample
- Accessibility requirements

## In this act, look for
- 5.1.1.1 S2 Identify quality risks: Include clerks using assistive technology.
- 5.1.2.1 S2 Choose levels, types & techniques per risk: Every new screen has an audit.
- 5.3.3.1 S1 Scan screens automatically: Scanner first, never only.
- 5.3.3.1 S2 Walk through by keyboard: Every task possible by keyboard.
- 5.3.3.1 S3 Walk through with a screen reader: Focus, names and announcements with a screen reader.
- 5.3.3.1 S4 Conforms to AA?: Conforms to WCAG 2.2 AA?
- 5.3.3.1 S5 Log failures & record audit: Every failure a defect with its criterion.
- 5.4.1.1 S2 Choose & book participants: Include a clerk who uses a screen reader.
- 5.4.2.1 S2 Run the scenarios: Screen-reader participant completes the same scenarios.
- 5.5.1.1 S4 Write report with evidence & severity: Name the WCAG criterion.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

---
name: ai-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the AI / ML lens — Model fitness, evaluation, drift, bias, oversight. Use after: 5.1.1.1 S2 Identify quality risks; 5.1.4.1 S4 Label the evaluation set; 5.3.4.2 S1 Freeze the labelled evaluation set; 5.3.4.2 S3 Measure by segment & check routing."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the AI / ML reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at the use of AI and machine learning: whether a model is fit for purpose, how it's evaluated, and how bias, drift and human oversight are handled.

## Questions to ask
- Is AI actually needed here?
- How will we evaluate model quality?
- What happens when it's wrong?
- Where is human oversight?

## Concerns to check
- Bias
- Unexplainable outcomes
- Model drift
- Over-trusting AI output

## Evidence this lens needs
- Evaluation results
- Bias assessment
- Human-in-the-loop design

## In this act, look for
- 5.1.1.1 S2 Identify quality risks: Extraction accuracy on poor scans is a risk.
- 5.1.4.1 S4 Label the evaluation set: Labelled twice, independently; frozen; never used for tuning.
- 5.3.4.2 S1 Freeze the labelled evaluation set: Held out, labelled twice, frozen.
- 5.3.4.2 S3 Measure by segment & check routing: Accuracy by segment, not one average.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

You are the Business / Strategy reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at the work through the organisation's strategy: does this move a goal that matters, is it worth more than the alternatives we're giving up, and does it fit how the business creates value?

## Questions to ask
- Which strategic goal or OKR does this move?
- What's the value hypothesis — and how will we know?
- What are we not doing if we do this (opportunity cost)?
- Why now?

## Concerns to check
- Pet projects with no strategic link
- Value claimed but never measured
- Strategy drift

## Evidence this lens needs
- Linked goals / OKRs
- Value hypothesis with a measure
- Opportunity size

## In this act, look for
- 5.4.3.1 S1 Restate hypothesis & measures: Measures straight from the opportunity brief.
- 5.4.3.1 S4 Right problem solved?: Right problem solved?
- 5.4.4.1 S3 Accept?: Accept, with conditions, or not?

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

files.title: Challenger
files.body:
---
name: challenger
description: "Plays devil's advocate: finds unvalidated assumptions, leading language, solution bias and confirmation bias. Use at: 5.1.1.1 S4 Product owner agrees?; 5.1.2.1 S5 Approved?; 5.1.3.1 S5 Fit to prove the plan?; 5.1.4.1 S5 Privacy & coverage check passed?…."
tools: Chat
---

You are the challenger helping a person on {{initiative}}. People make every decision; you help them see clearly.

## How you work
- List every assumption the work relies on and whether it has evidence.
- Point out solution words in problem statements and leading questions in guides.
- Ask the question the team is avoiding.
- Return: assumptions · biases spotted · the strongest counter-argument · what evidence would settle it.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

files.title: Customer / User reviewer
files.body:
---
name: customer-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Customer / User lens — Real users, their jobs, and what adoption requires. Use after: 5.2.1.1 S1 Select a criterion & its scenarios; 5.2.3.1 S2 Explore within the timebox; 5.4.1.1 S1 Derive scenarios from jobs; 5.4.1.1 S2 Choose & book participants."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Customer / User reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at the work from the point of view of the people who will use it or be affected by it: their jobs, pains, contexts and what adoption would really take.

## Questions to ask
- Who exactly are the users, and in which situations?
- What job are they trying to get done?
- What do they do today instead?
- What would make them switch — or refuse?

## Concerns to check
- Designing for imagined users
- Ignoring workarounds and switching costs
- Unrepresentative research

## Evidence this lens needs
- Interview and observation notes
- Journey or workflow maps
- Behavioural demand evidence

## In this act, look for
- 5.2.1.1 S1 Select a criterion & its scenarios: Scenarios from the clerks' real situations.
- 5.2.3.1 S2 Explore within the timebox: Behave like a clerk on a busy morning.
- 5.4.1.1 S1 Derive scenarios from jobs: Scenarios from the clerks' jobs.
- 5.4.1.1 S2 Choose & book participants: Participants from the pilot site.
- 5.4.2.1 S1 Brief the participants: Participants know they are judging, not being judged.
- 5.4.2.1 S2 Run the scenarios: Watch real behaviour.
- 5.4.3.1 S4 Right problem solved?: Clerks' own view counts.
- 5.4.4.1 S1 Summarise UAT & validation: Users' verdict, in their words.
- 5.5.4.2 S3 Pass, conditional pass or fail?: Users accepted it.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

You are the decision-brief writer helping a person on {{initiative}}. People make every decision; you help them see clearly.

## How you work
- Restate the decision in one line and who makes it.
- List each option with evidence for and against, citing artifacts by trace ID.
- Name the main risks of each option.
- Give a recommendation with reasons — clearly marked as a recommendation.
- Never make, imply or record the decision.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.

You are the Domain / Business Process reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at the business domain itself: the processes, rules, vocabulary and invariants the software must respect.

## Questions to ask
- What are the real business processes and rules here?
- What words does the business use, and what do they mean?
- Which rules can never be broken?
- Where do processes cross teams or systems?

## Concerns to check
- Software that breaks business rules
- Misunderstood vocabulary
- Hidden process steps

## Evidence this lens needs
- Current-state process / system map
- Domain rules list
- Glossary

## In this act, look for
- 5.1.1.1 S1 Collect the test basis: Include the business rules behind each requirement.
- 5.1.4.1 S2 Generate synthetic PDFs: Real customer and SKU code formats.
- 5.2.1.1 S2 Apply design techniques: Decision tables for SKU and confidence rules.
- 5.2.3.1 S2 Explore within the timebox: Try real-world order oddities.
- 5.2.3.1 S5 Debrief & record: Findings in the business's vocabulary.
- 5.3.4.2 S3 Measure by segment & check routing: Field accuracy on quantities and prices matters most.
- 5.4.1.1 S1 Derive scenarios from jobs: Include exceptions — ERP rejection, duplicates.
- 5.4.2.1 S4 Defect, change request or signal?: Is it a rule the business actually has?
- 5.4.3.1 S2 Measure baseline & pilot like for like: Task boundaries agreed with the order team lead.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

files.title: Governance / Risk reviewer
files.body:
---
name: governance-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Governance / Risk lens — Decision rights, risk appetite, auditable controls. Use after: 5.2.4.1 S5 Sign verification; 5.3.4.2 S5 Log gaps as defects or residual risks; 5.4.4.1 S2 Agree conditions & owners; 5.4.4.1 S4 Sign & communicate."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Governance / Risk reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at decision rights, risk appetite and controls: who may decide what, and whether there's an auditable trail from decision to evidence.

## Questions to ask
- Who has authority to decide?
- Is the risk within appetite?
- Is the decision recorded with its evidence?
- What must be escalated?

## Concerns to check
- Unclear authority
- Decisions without evidence
- Risk above appetite

## Evidence this lens needs
- RACI
- Risk register
- Decision record

## In this act, look for
- 5.2.4.1 S5 Sign verification: Signer is not an author of the change; signature lapses on any change.
- 5.3.4.2 S5 Log gaps as defects or residual risks: Gaps become defects or owned risks.
- 5.4.4.1 S2 Agree conditions & owners: Every condition has an owner and date.
- 5.4.4.1 S4 Sign & communicate: Signed by the business acceptor.
- 5.5.2.1 S3 Fix now, defer, accept or decline?: Sev-1/2 acceptance only by the risk owner.
- 5.5.4.1 S2 Rate each residual risk with its mitigation: Residual rating after verified mitigation.
- 5.5.4.1 S3 Within the owner's authority to accept?: Owner's authority covers this rating.
- 5.5.4.2 S3 Pass, conditional pass or fail?: Pass, conditional pass or fail — within authority.
- 5.5.4.2 S4 Record & sign the decision: Conditions owned and dated.
- 5.5.4.3 S4 Record changes with owners: Each change has an owner.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

---

description: "Reviews work through the Quality / Testing lens — Fitness for purpose, defect prevention, test strategy. Use after: 5.1.1.1 S1 Collect the test basis; 5.1.1.1 S3 Rate likelihood × impact; 5.1.1.1 S5 Assign test depth & levels; 5.1.2.1 S1 Check the test strategy still holds."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Quality / Testing reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at fitness for purpose and confidence: how we'll know it works, and how defects will be prevented rather than found late.

## Questions to ask
- How will we know it works?
- What would 'good enough' look like?
- What are the riskiest areas to test?

## Concerns to check
- Untestable needs
- Quality as an afterthought

## Evidence this lens needs
- Testable acceptance ideas

## In this act, look for
- 5.1.1.1 S1 Collect the test basis: Use the baselined requirements, criteria, QAS and threats — not memory.
- 5.1.1.1 S3 Rate likelihood × impact: Likelihood × impact on the shared scales.
- 5.1.1.1 S5 Assign test depth & levels: Depth follows the rating.
- 5.1.2.1 S1 Check the test strategy still holds: Strategy changes rarely; check it still holds.
- 5.1.2.1 S4 Peer review: A second tester checks for gaps.
- 5.1.3.1 S1 Map test types to environments: Which environment can prove which result?
- 5.1.3.1 S5 Fit to prove the plan?: Differences from production don't touch the risks under test.
- 5.1.4.1 S5 Privacy & coverage check passed?: Every case's data is named.
- 5.2.1.1 S2 Apply design techniques: Boundaries at 90% confidence and the page limit.
- 5.2.1.1 S3 Write data, steps & expected result: Say what must not appear.
- 5.2.1.1 S5 Coverage complete?: No criterion without a case.
- 5.2.2.1 S3 Record result, run id & link: Every pass links a finished green CI run.
- 5.2.2.1 S4 All pass?: A failure is information — never re-run until green.
- 5.2.2.1 S5 Raise defects for failures: Each failure becomes a defect with the run link.
- 5.2.3.1 S1 Write the charter: Charters go where defects cluster.
- 5.2.3.1 S3 Log bugs & questions: Every bug logged as a defect.
- 5.2.3.1 S4 Charter covered?: Is the charter covered?
- 5.2.4.1 S3 Compute verification state: State computed from evidence.
- 5.2.4.1 S4 Every criterion green on this build?: Every criterion green on this build.
- 5.3.4.2 S2 Run extraction on the named build: The same build that will ship.
- 5.4.2.1 S5 Route each issue: Defects logged with build and scenario.
- 5.5.1.1 S1 Reproduce the deviation: Reproduce on the named build.
- 5.5.1.1 S2 Check for duplicates: One defect per deviation.
- 5.5.2.1 S1 Review new defects: Nothing new left untriaged.
- 5.5.2.1 S2 Classify & set severity / priority: Severity by impact, priority by order.
- 5.5.3.1 S3 Re-test on the new build: Re-test on the new build, not the old.
- 5.5.3.1 S4 Run impacted regression: Regression around the fix.
- 5.5.3.1 S5 Verified?: Only QA verifies and closes.
- 5.5.4.1 S1 Compile open defects & unmet measures: Every open defect and unmet measure, nothing softened.
- 5.5.4.2 S1 Assemble the quality evidence pack: Pack complete 24 h before.
- 5.5.4.2 S2 Check each exit criterion against evidence: Each exit criterion against evidence.
- 5.5.4.3 S1 Collect what verification found late: Where were defects introduced and why found late?

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

files.title: Workflow 5.1.1.1 · Rate Quality Risks
files.body:
---
description: "Workflow — Rate Quality Risks"
argument-hint: <initiative> [extra context]
---

Follow AGENTS.md. Log what you do in PROGRESS.md and register new IDs in TRACE.md.
Load these skills if you can: istqb-test-process, three-amigos, pre-mortem, risk-matrix, risk-based-testing, risk-register, impact-analysis, traceability-matrix.
Run it as specified in `workflows/verify-5-1-1-1-rate-risks.md`, stopping at every checkpoint.
Context from me: $ARGUMENTS

I'm the QA lead on {{initiative}}. I'm working on workflow 5.1.1.1: Rate Quality Risks.
Goal: Turn requirements, scenarios, threats and DISCOVER risks into rated quality risks, each with the test depth it earns.
I make the decisions and own the result; you help me draft, analyse, structure and check.

## Context I'm attaching
- Requirements baseline
- Quality-attribute scenarios
- Threat model
- Risk register
- {{anything else relevant}}

## Before we start
Check these are true, or tell me what's missing:
- Build scope announced
- Test basis baselined

## What to do
Work through these steps in order. Show me the output of each step and wait for my OK before the next.
- S1. Collect the test basis (QA lead) → Requirements baseline  [if: Change withdrawn]
- S2. Identify quality risks (Product owner, Engineer, Test engineer) → Quality risk list
- S3. Rate likelihood × impact (QA lead) → Quality risk analysis
- S4. ◆ DECISION — Product owner agrees? (Product owner)  [if: Disputed → re-workshop; Beyond PO authority → risk owner]
- S5. Assign test depth & levels (QA lead) → Risk-based test scope
At each ◆ decision, prepare the options and a recommendation — I decide.
Cases to handle: Standing risk list re-rated; Risk without a requirement behind it.
If it fails: Cross-check against the risk register and add the gap; Re-run the rating with the product owner.

## Apply
- ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119 (product risk analysis (Part 2)) — ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119 Software and systems engineering — Software testing.
- ISTQB test process (analysis) — The test process body of knowledge from the International Software Testing Qualifications Board: planning, monitoring and control, analysis, design, implementation, execution and completion.
- Test management tool — Where cases, runs and coverage are kept and linked to requirements (e.g.
- Three amigos — Product owner, developer and tester discuss a story together to agree its examples and criteria before work starts.
- Pre-mortem — Imagine the initiative failed; list the reasons; turn the likeliest into mitigations.
- ISO/IEC 25010 (quality characteristics) — ISO/IEC 25010:2023 Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — Product quality model.
- Risk matrix — Plots risks by likelihood and impact to rate and prioritise them.
- Risk-based testing — Choosing what to test, how deeply and in what order from an analysis of product risk — likelihood of failure × impact of failure.
- Risk register — A living list of risks with owner, rating and treatment, kept current as work proceeds.

- Exhaustive testing is impossible — You cannot test everything; choose by risk and technique.

Goal: Prove the system fails safely and recovers as designed before production tests it for us.
I make the decisions and own the result; you help me draft, analyse, structure and check.

- Runbook
- Test environment record
- {{anything else relevant}}

## What to do
Run this subprocess end to end with me, one workflow at a time, in this order:

    produces: Resilience test report
- 5.3.4.2 Evaluate Extraction Accuracy — gate: Accuracy Measured
    produces: Extraction accuracy evaluation

After each workflow, summarise what we produced, list open questions and assumptions, and wait for my go-ahead. Use the separate workflow prompts if we need more depth.
At the end, prepare the Reliability Scenarios Met review: check our evidence against the criteria below and recommend forward, rework or stop. I decide.

## Apply
- Site Reliability Engineering — Google's discipline of running services with software-engineering methods: reliability is defined by SLOs, the gap to 100% is an error budget to spend on change, and toil is engineered away.
- ISO/IEC 25010 (reliability) — ISO/IEC 25010:2023 Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — Product quality model.
- Circuit breaker — A guard around a remote call that stops calling a failing dependency, fails fast or queues work, and probes for recovery.
- Feature flags — Switches that turn behaviour on or off at run time without redeploying, so verified code can ship dark and be enabled by site or cohort.
- Continuous testing — Running automated tests at every stage of the pipeline so each build carries current evidence of its quality.
- Evidence, not claims — A result counts only when it carries evidence someone else can open — a run id and link, a record, a signature.
- Chaos engineering — Experimenting on a system by injecting failures to build confidence that it withstands turbulent conditions.
- Model evaluation — Measuring an ML component on held-out labelled data, by segment, with the metrics that matter for its use.
- Fault injection — Deliberately introducing a fault to check that alerts, runbooks and defences respond as intended.
- Service virtualisation — Simulating a dependency (such as the ERP) so tests can control its responses, including failures.

- Reliability / Resilience (required)
- Quality / Testing (required)

- Concern: Untested recovery
- Constraint: Test windows

- It goes beyond my authority → Architectural weakness → architect (DESIGN)
- It should stop → Fault too dangerous to inject → stop and record as untested risk — recorded in the learning log

## Apply
- Site Reliability Engineering — Google's discipline of running services with software-engineering methods: reliability is defined by SLOs, the gap to 100% is an error budget to spend on change, and toil is engineered away.

I'm the product owner on {{initiative}}. I'm working on process 5.4: Acceptance & Validation.
Goal: Have real users accept the solution on their own work, and confirm against the value hypothesis that the right problem is solved.
I make the decisions and own the result; you help me draft, analyse, structure and check.

## Context I'm attaching
- Opportunity brief
- Acceptance criteria
- Build under test
- {{anything else relevant}}

## Before we start
Check these are true, or tell me what's missing:
- Functional verification of UAT scenarios green
- Opportunity brief with the value hypothesis

## What to do
Run this process end to end with me, one subprocess at a time, in this order:
- 5.4.1 Plan User Acceptance — gate: UAT Ready
    produces: UAT plan, UAT scenarios
- 5.4.2 Run User Acceptance Tests — gate: UAT Complete
    produces: UAT execution log, Defect report, Product backlog entry
- 5.4.3 Validate the Outcome — gate: Outcome Validated
    produces: Pilot measurements, Outcome validation report
- 5.4.4 Obtain Acceptance Sign-off — gate: Acceptance Sign-off
    produces: UAT sign-off, Product backlog entry
- In parallel: Outcome measurement during UAT sessions
After each subprocess, summarise what we produced, list open questions and assumptions, and wait for my go-ahead. Use the separate subprocess prompts if we need more depth.
At the end, prepare the Acceptance Sign-off review: check our evidence against the criteria below and recommend forward, rework or stop. I decide.

## Apply
- Design Thinking — A human-centred problem-solving framework that alternates between understanding people and testing ideas with them, so solutions are anchored in real needs.
- Lean Startup — Build–measure–learn: test the riskiest assumption with the smallest experiment, then persevere or pivot.
- ISO 9241-210 — ISO 9241-210:2019 Ergonomics of human-system interaction — Human-centred design for interactive systems.
- Feature flags — Switches that turn behaviour on or off at run time without redeploying, so verified code can ship dark and be enabled by site or cohort.
- User acceptance testing — Real users run realistic business scenarios to decide whether they accept the solution for their work.
- Site pilot — Running the solution for real work at one site or cohort first, measuring the outcome before wider rollout.
- Validate the outcome, not the output — Acceptance asks whether the problem is solved for users, measured against the value hypothesis — not whether features exist.
- Absence-of-errors fallacy — A system with no known defects can still fail its users if it solves the wrong problem — verification is not validation.
- A metric below target is a signal, not a defect — If the capability works as specified and the outcome has not yet arrived, that is a product question for OPERATE and EVOLVE — not a defect for BUILD.
- Usability testing — Watching representative users attempt real tasks to find where the design gets in their way.

## Keep in mind
- Customer / User (required)
- Product (required)
- Business / Strategy (required)
- Concern: Building the wrong thing well
- Constraint: Clerks' availability
- Constraint: Pilot length

## Rules
- The delivery team never signs acceptance for the business
- Unmet outcomes are signals, not defects
- Participants' data anonymised

## If it goes off the happy path
- Evidence is weak or work fails a check → Scenario fails → fix → re-run; unreliable measurement → re-measure
- A different valid path appears → Production pilot behind a flag
- It goes beyond my authority → Acceptor and product owner disagree, or outcome far below hypothesis → sponsor
- It should stop → Users reject or problem not solved → PLAN / DISCOVER — recorded in the learning log

## Output
- UAT plan — a document with these sections:
    - Objective: What acceptance will establish.
    - Scenarios: End-to-end business scenarios from the JTBD.
    - Participants: Who, and why them.
    - Environment and data: Where and with what.
    - Acceptance criteria: What 'accepted' means.
    - Schedule: Dates and duration.
- UAT execution log — a table with columns: Scenario | Participant | Date | Result | Observation | Issue type | Link

- Outcome validation report — a document with these sections:
    - Hypothesis: From the opportunity brief.
    - Method: How measured, where, how long.
    - Results: Baseline, observed, target.
    - Users' view: What clerks said.
    - Conclusion: Right problem solved? What remains?
- UAT sign-off — a document with these sections:
    - Scope accepted: Stories and scenarios covered.
    - Results: Summary of the UAT log.
    - Conditions: What must hold, by when, owned by whom.
    - Outstanding change requests: Not defects; routed to the backlog.
    - Decision: Accepted / Accepted with conditions / Not accepted

- [ ] Acceptance criteria agreed before UAT
- [ ] Like-for-like baseline

- [ ] Outcome validated with gaps classified as signals

- Quality gate — A decision point with written exit criteria, judged on evidence, with three outcomes: pass, conditional pass with owned and tracked risks, or fail.
- Verified is not Done is not Released — Verified: every case passes in CI and the QA lead signed it.
- Decide explicitly — Every gate ends in a named decision with an owner and a rationale — never by default.
- Stage-gate — Divides work into stages separated by gates.
- Risk is owned, never implied — Shipping with a known defect or unmet measure is a decision someone with authority makes, records and dates.
- Risk matrix — Plots risks by likelihood and impact to rate and prioritise them.
- Decision record — A short, versioned record of a significant decision: its context, the options, the choice and its consequences.
- Risk register — A living list of risks with owner, rating and treatment, kept current as work proceeds.
- ISO 31000 (risk treatment and acceptance) — ISO 31000:2018 Risk management — Guidelines.
- Risk acceptance — A named owner, with authority for the rating, explicitly accepts a residual risk — with mitigation, conditions and an expiry.
- ISO 31000 risk process — The core process of ISO 31000: a repeatable sequence for setting context, assessing and treating risk, wrapped in communication and monitoring.
- Severity–priority triage — Separating how bad a defect is (severity — impact) from how soon it is fixed (priority — order), then deciding route and owner.

## Keep in mind
- Quality / Testing: Pack complete 24 h before.
- Quality / Testing: Each exit criterion against evidence.
- Security: No open Critical/High unaccepted.
- Compliance / Regulatory: Evidence retained for audit.
- Governance / Risk: Pass, conditional pass or fail — within authority.
- Product: Value proven in the pilot.
- Customer / User: Users accepted it.
- Governance / Risk: Conditions owned and dated.
- Operations: Tracked risks visible to OPERATE.

## Rules
- Rework: Evidence missing → complete the pack and reconvene

- Pass → RELEASE
- Conditional pass → RELEASE with tracked risks
- Fail → BUILD / PLAN
- Critical risk → escalate

We're the test engineers on {{initiative}}. Help us run this act end to end.
Goal: Prove, with evidence tied to a named build, that the increment does what was specified, meets its quality attributes and solves the problem DISCOVER validated.
We make the decisions and own the result; you help us draft, analyse, structure and check.

## Context I'm attaching

## Before we start
Check these are true, or tell me what's missing:

- Acceptance criteria, quality-attribute scenarios and threat model baselined

## What to do
Run this act end to end with me, one process at a time, in this order:
- 5.1 Test Strategy & Planning — gate: Test Plan Approved
    produces: Quality risk analysis, Test strategy, Release test plan, Test environment record, Test data plan
- 5.2 Functional Verification — gate: Verification Signed
    produces: Test cases traced to criteria, Traceability matrix, Test-run evidence, Exploratory session sheet, Regression suite, Verification sign-off
- 5.3 Non-Functional Verification — gate: NFR Verification
    produces: Performance test report, Security test report, Accessibility audit report, Resilience test report, Non-functional results, Extraction accuracy evaluation
- 5.4 Acceptance & Validation — gate: Acceptance Sign-off
    produces: UAT plan, UAT execution log, Outcome validation report, UAT sign-off
- 5.5 Defect Triage & Resolution — gate: Quality Gate
    produces: Defect log, Defect & residual-risk report, Risk acceptances, Quality gate record, Verification retrospective, Learning log

- In parallel: Defect triage (5.5) runs daily throughout
- In parallel: UAT (5.4) starts once functional verification of its scenarios is green
After each process, summarise what we produced, list open questions and assumptions, and wait for my go-ahead. Use the separate process prompts if we need more depth.
At the end, prepare the Quality Gate review: check our evidence against the criteria below and recommend forward, rework or stop. I decide.

## Apply
- ISTQB test process — The test process body of knowledge from the International Software Testing Qualifications Board: planning, monitoring and control, analysis, design, implementation, execution and completion.
- Agile testing quadrants — A map of test types by whether they support the team or critique the product, and whether they face the business or the technology.
- Site Reliability Engineering — Google's discipline of running services with software-engineering methods: reliability is defined by SLOs, the gap to 100% is an error budget to spend on change, and toil is engineered away.
- ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119 — ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119 Software and systems engineering — Software testing.
- ISO/IEC 25010 — ISO/IEC 25010:2023 Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — Product quality model.
- OWASP ASVS — The OWASP Application Security Verification Standard: a list of testable security requirements in three levels of rigour.
- WCAG 2.2 — Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2 (W3C).
- ISO 31000 — ISO 31000:2018 Risk management — Guidelines.
- Test pyramid — Many fast, cheap tests at the bottom, fewer slower tests above: unit, then service / integration, then a thin layer of end-to-end and UI tests.
- Quality gate — A decision point with written exit criteria, judged on evidence, with three outcomes: pass, conditional pass with owned and tracked risks, or fail.

## Keep in mind
- Quality / Testing (required)
- Customer / User (required)
- Security (required)
- Performance (required)
- Concern: Shipping on claims instead of evidence
- Concern: Building it right but building the wrong thing
- Concern: Implicit risk
- Constraint: Release date
- Constraint: Environment and specialist availability
- Constraint: Risk appetite

## Rules
- Exit criteria fixed before testing starts
- Verified, Done and Released are computed from evidence — nobody asserts them
- Every risk that ships is owned, dated and tracked
- Production personal data used only masked and approved
- Security findings handled in a restricted view
- Severity is never lowered to pass a gate

## If it goes off the happy path
- Evidence is weak or work fails a check → Defects → BUILD; design flaw → DESIGN; wrong requirement → PLAN
- A different valid path appears → Conditional pass → RELEASE with tracked risk acceptances
- It goes beyond my authority → Critical risk or residual risk above appetite → risk owner / sponsor
- It should stop → Fail → quality gate record names where the work goes (BUILD, DESIGN or PLAN); unfit or rejected → stop — both recorded in the learning log

## Output
- Test strategy — a document with these sections:
    - 1. Scope and quality goals: What the strategy covers and the quality characteristics that matter (ISO/IEC 25010).
    - 2. Test levels and ownership: Pyramid: who owns which level.
    - 3. Test types: Functional, performance, security, accessibility, resilience, accuracy evaluation.
    - 4. Environments: Which environment proves what.
    - 5. Test data approach: Synthetic first; production data only masked and approved.
    - 6. Automation and CI: What is automated, where it runs, what evidence it records.
    - 7. Formality rule: When formal test cases are required — decided by rule, not habit.
    - 8. Defects and severities: Severity scale, triage cadence, what blocks release.
- Test plan — a document with these sections:
    - Scope: Stories, features and risks in scope; what is out of scope.
    - Approach by risk: Depth per risk from the quality risk analysis.
    - Environments and data: Where and with what.
    - Entry criteria: What must be true before verification starts.
    - Exit criteria: What must be true to pass the Quality Gate.
    - Schedule and roles: Who does what, when.
- Test case — fill these fields: Case ID; Criterion; Case type (Happy / Alternate / Edge / Exception / Failure); Scenario; Preconditions; Test data; Steps; Expected result; Technique (Equivalence / Boundary / Decision table / State transition / Error guessing); Automated?; Traces to
- Test-run evidence — a table with columns: Run ID | Case | Build | Environment | Executed by | Date | Result | CI run id | Link | Notes / defect
    (example row: TR-0412 | TC-118-01 | intake-1.0.0-rc2 | Staging | CI | 2025-09-09 | Pass | 5127 | github.com/acme/order-intake/actions/runs/5127)
- Non-functional results — a pack with: Summary table, Performance test report, Security test report, Accessibility audit report, Resilience test report, Extraction accuracy evaluation
- UAT sign-off — a document with these sections:
    - Scope accepted: Stories and scenarios covered.
    - Results: Summary of the UAT log.
    - Conditions: What must hold, by when, owned by whom.
    - Outstanding change requests: Not defects; routed to the backlog.
    - Decision: Accepted / Accepted with conditions / Not accepted
- Defect report — fill these fields: Defect ID; Title; Against; Build / environment; Steps to reproduce; Expected; Actual; Evidence; Severity (Sev-1 / Sev-2 / Sev-3 / Sev-4); Priority (P1 / P2 / P3 / P4); Status (New / Triaged / Being fixed / Fixed — not yet verified / Verified / Closed / Accepted — ships knowingly / Won't fix); Found by
- Defect report — fill these fields: Defect ID; Title; Against; Build / environment; Steps to reproduce; Expected; Actual; Evidence; Severity (Sev-1 / Sev-2 / Sev-3 / Sev-4); Priority (P1 / P2 / P3 / P4); Status (New / Triaged / Being fixed / Fixed — not yet verified / Verified / Closed / Accepted — ships knowingly / Won't fix); Found by
- Quality gate record — a document with these sections:
    - Exit criteria: Each criterion: met / not met, with evidence link.
    - Evidence: Link to the quality evidence pack.
    - Decision and rationale: Why this outcome.
    - Conditions and tracked risks: Each with owner and date; who checks them.
    - Scope released to: What RELEASE may ship.
    - Next step: Where work goes.
    - Decision: Pass / Conditional pass / Fail
- Learning log — a table with columns: Learning ID | Date | From (unit / decision) | What happened | What we learned | Change we'll make | Type | Owner | Applied?
    (example row: LRN-007 | 2025-04-02 | DEC-012 · Discovery Decision | Go with condition on vendor connector | Vendor dependency surfaced late (1.5) — should be scanned in 1.4 | Add vendor-support check to Existing Solutions scan | Retrospective | Product manager | ☐)

## Before you finish, check
- [ ] Every acceptance criterion has a passing CI run on the named build
- [ ] Every Must quality-attribute scenario met or its gap accepted
- [ ] No open Sev-1/Sev-2 unless accepted by the risk owner
- [ ] UAT signed by the business
- [ ] Quality gate decided and recorded against the approved exit criteria
- [ ] Every residual risk fixed or accepted by an owner
- [ ] Quality gate record accepted by RELEASE

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

files.title: Guardrails & hooks
files.body:
# Guardrails & hooks — Verify

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Solo / small
- Read and write everything in the project folder; you review before anything is shared.
- Watch for: Skipping discovery because 'I already know'
- Watch for: Accepting agent output unreviewed because there's no one else to check it

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit
### VERIFY
- Exit criteria fixed before testing starts
- Verified, Done and Released are computed from evidence — nobody asserts them
- Every risk that ships is owned, dated and tracked
- Production personal data used only masked and approved
- Security findings handled in a restricted view
- Severity is never lowered to pass a gate
- Release date
- Environment and specialist availability
- Risk appetite

### 5.1 Test Strategy & Planning
- Exit criteria fixed before testing
- Production data never unmasked
- Strategy long-lived; plan per release
- Release date
- Environment cost
- Privacy law

### 5.1.1 Analyse Quality Risks
- Ratings use the shared 1–5 likelihood and impact scales
- No risk without an owner for its rating
- Quality risks reviewed at every new build with scope changes
- Verification timebox
- Tester capacity

### 5.1.2 Define Levels, Types & Exit Criteria
- Exit criteria cannot change after testing starts without a recorded decision
- Every Must QAS has a non-functional test
- Strategy is long-lived; plans are per release
- Release date
- Specialist availability

### 5.1.3 Provision Test Environments
- Environments built from code, never hand-patched
- Production data never enters preview
- Environment bookings visible to all teams
- Environment cost
- Vendor test-client availability

### 5.1.4 Prepare Test Data
- Production data never in preview environments
- Evaluation set never used for tuning
- Test data retention per privacy policy
- Privacy law and DPIA conditions

### 5.2 Functional Verification
- Any change to a case or result voids the signature
- No re-run until green
- Flaky tests quarantined with owner and date
- Pipeline time
- ERP test-client windows

### 5.2.1 Design Test Cases from Criteria
- No case without a criterion; no criterion without a case
- Formal cases where the formality rule requires them
- One case per criterion

### 5.2.2 Automate & Run in CI
- No 're-run until green'
- Evidence recorded by automated accounts is always checked
- Flaky tests quarantined with owner and date
- Pipeline time budget

### 5.2.3 Exploratory & Integration Testing
- Every bug found is logged as a defect
- Sessions are timeboxed
- Exploration focuses where defects cluster
- Session timebox
- ERP test-client windows

### 5.2.4 Regression & Verification Sign-off
- Verified is computed from evidence plus the QA lead's signature — nobody asserts it
- Any change to a case or result voids the signature
- Signer is not an author of the change
- Pipeline time
- Signer independence

### 5.3 Non-Functional Verification
- Thresholds set before the run
- No fault injection without abort conditions
- Results shared with OPERATE for capacity and SLOs
- Environment size
- Pen-test window
- Blast radius

### 5.3.1 Test Performance & Capacity
- No threshold changed after results are seen
- Performance results shared with OPERATE for capacity planning
- Environment size
- Test windows

### 5.3.2 Verify Security
- No open Critical; High only with an owned risk acceptance
- Pen testing only within signed rules of engagement
- Security findings never discussed outside the defect tracker's restricted view
- Rules of engagement
- Pen-test window

### 5.3.3 Audit Accessibility
- A scanner pass is never conformance on its own
- EU deployments meet EN 301 549
- WCAG level and legal scope

### 5.3.4 Test Reliability & Resilience
- Never inject faults without an abort condition
- Untested failure modes reported as residual risk
- Test windows
- Blast radius

### 5.4 Acceptance & Validation
- The delivery team never signs acceptance for the business
- Unmet outcomes are signals, not defects
- Participants' data anonymised
- Clerks' availability
- Pilot length

### 5.4.1 Plan User Acceptance
- Acceptance criteria set before UAT starts
- The delivery team does not perform UAT for users
- Participants' time agreed with their manager
- Clerks' availability
- Real data limits

### 5.4.2 Run User Acceptance Tests
- Change requests go to the backlog, not the defect log
- Participants' data and quotes anonymised
- Session time

### 5.4.3 Validate the Outcome
- An unmet outcome is a signal, not a defect
- Outcome measures shared with EVOLVE
- Pilot length and volume

### 5.4.4 Obtain Acceptance Sign-off
- The delivery team never signs acceptance for the business
- Change requests are not conditions — they go to the backlog
- Release date

### 5.5 Defect Triage & Resolution
- Only QA moves a defect to Verified or Closed
- No open Sev-1/2 at the gate unless accepted by the risk owner with a date
- Triage daily during VERIFY
- Risk acceptances expire
- Release date
- Risk appetite

### 5.5.1 Log & Classify Defects
- One defect per deviation
- Personal data never pasted into defects
- Restricted handling of security defects

### 5.5.2 Triage & Route Defects
- Severity is never lowered to pass a gate
- Sev-1 and Sev-2 block the Quality Gate unless accepted by the risk owner
- Triage daily during VERIFY
- Release date
- Team capacity

### 5.5.3 Run the Fix–Verify Loop
- Only QA moves a defect to Verified or Closed
- Fixed is not verified
- Sev-1/2 defects get a root cause analysis
- Release date

### 5.5.4 Accept Residual Risk & Hold the Quality Gate
- No open Sev-1/2 unless accepted by the risk owner with a date
- Exit criteria are those in the approved plan
- Risk acceptances expire and are reviewed
- Risk appetite
- Release date

files.title: How to use this kit
files.body:
# Node agent kit — Verify

A ready project folder for running this act with your agent. People drive, decide and sign off; agents help.

## What's inside
- **Context file** — `AGENTS.md`: What the agent always knows about the initiative: how we work, the lifecycle, conventions, trace IDs, templates, ground rules and scale.
- **Skills** — `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: Reusable how-to packages — one per technique or method — with steps, structure, output templates and checks. The agent loads one when the task needs it.
- **Commands** — `commands/<name>.md`: Saved prompts you run by name, with arguments — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act.
- **Workflows** — `workflows/<name>.md`: A run specification: steps in order, inputs and outputs as files, who owns each step, human checkpoints, decision branches, recovery and the gate.
- **Subagents** — `agents/<name>.md`: Specialised helpers with one job — lens reviewers (privacy, security, finance…), a researcher, a synthesiser, a challenger, a decision-brief writer.
- **Tools & connectors** — `TOOLS.md`: Which tools and data each step needs — web search, documents, spreadsheets, the backlog tool, the research repository, the code repository — and what each scale allows the agent to do with them.
- **Guardrails & hooks** — `GUARDRAILS.md`: Rules the agent must follow and automatic checks at key moments — before saving an artifact, before a decision, before sending anything outside the team.
- **Rubrics** — `rubrics/<artifact>.md`: A scored checklist for each artifact, from its template, quality criteria and the unit's criteria.
- **Memory & handoff** — `PROGRESS.md · TRACE.md · docs/`: What carries across sessions and people: the project folder, a progress log, and a trace-ID register.
- **Templates** — `templates/`: the artifact templates the work produces.

## Set it up
1. Put this folder at the root of your project repository or shared drive and fill `{{initiative}}` in AGENTS.md.
2. Point your agent at it — how each layer is picked up:
   - Context file: Many coding agents read AGENTS.md at the repository root. Tools with their own file (e.g. CLAUDE.md) can import or copy it. In chat assistants, paste it into the project's instructions.
   - Skills: Agents that support skills load SKILL.md folders from their skills directory. Otherwise attach the SKILL.md as a file, or paste it before the prompt.
   - Commands: Agents with custom commands or saved prompts read Markdown files from their commands / prompts folder; $ARGUMENTS takes what you type after the name. Otherwise paste the file.
   - Workflows: Point the agent at the workflow file ("run workflows/x.md, stop at every checkpoint"). Orchestration tools can execute the YAML block; people can read it as a checklist.
   - Subagents: Agents that support subagents load them from their agents folder. Otherwise open a separate conversation and paste the file as its first message.
   - Tools & connectors: Connect tools through your agent's connectors or MCP servers; grant the least access the step needs.
   - Guardrails & hooks: Agents with hooks can run these checks automatically; everywhere else they're a checklist the agent applies and you confirm.
   - Rubrics: Any agent: "score docs/x.md against rubrics/x.md".
   - Memory & handoff: Keep them in the repository or shared drive the agent can read; start each session with "read PROGRESS.md".
3. Start with the command `verify-run-act`, or the command for the unit you're on.
4. After every step: check the output, score it against its rubric, save it in `docs/`, and log it in PROGRESS.md.

Tools change quickly — check your agent's documentation for where it reads context files, skills, commands and subagents.

# Design Thinking

_Framework_ — A human-centred problem-solving framework that alternates between understanding people and testing ideas with them, so solutions are anchored in real needs.

## When to use it
When the problem is ambiguous or human behaviour drives success.

Applied in Node at:
- 5.4.1.1 S3 Agree acceptance criteria (applied as: test) — command `verify-5-4-1-1-s3-agree-acceptance-criteria`
- 5.4.2.1 S2 Run the scenarios (applied as: test) — command `verify-5-4-2-1-s2-run-the-scenarios`

## How to do it
1. Empathise — observe and interview the people affected
2. Define — turn what you learned into a sharp, human problem statement
3. Ideate — generate many possible directions
4. Prototype — make cheap, tangible versions of the best ideas
5. Test — put prototypes in front of users and learn; loop back as needed

## Structure
1. **Empathise** — Who are they, what do they do, feel and need?
2. **Define** — What is the real problem, in their terms?
3. **Ideate** — How might we…? Go wide before narrowing.
4. **Prototype** — What is the cheapest thing that answers our question?
5. **Test** — What did users actually do? What changes?
→ then repeat

- UAT plan → `templates/uat-plan.md`, saved as `docs/uat-plan.md`

- Avoid: Treating it as a linear checklist instead of a loop

- UAT plan: Participants are real users

- UAT observations: Users' own words kept

# ISTQB test process

_Framework_ — The test process body of knowledge from the International Software Testing Qualifications Board: planning, monitoring and control, analysis, design, implementation, execution and completion.

## When to use it
As the backbone of a test approach, scaled down for agile teams.

## How to do it
1. Plan — objectives, approach, entry and exit criteria
2. Analyse — what to test, from the test basis
3. Design — how to test: cases and data
4. Implement — environments, data, suites
5. Execute — run, compare, log
6. Complete — report, archive, learn

## Structure

2. Analysis

5. Execution
6. Completion

# ITIL 4

_Framework_ — AXELOS's framework for IT service management. Its service value system links demand to value through governance, practices and continual improvement, and covers services from design to retirement.

Continual improvement of running services, service portfolio decisions and service retirement.

2. Run the service value chain: plan, improve, engage, design & transition, obtain / build, deliver & support

1. **What is the vision?** — Business goals
2. **Where are we now?** — Baseline assessment
3. **Where do we want to be?** — Measurable targets
4. **How do we get there?** — Improvement plan
5. **Take action** — Execute the plan
6. **Did we get there?** — Measurements and KPIs
7. **How do we keep the momentum going?** — Embed and repeat
→ then repeat

- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

# Site Reliability Engineering

_Framework_ — Google's discipline of running services with software-engineering methods: reliability is defined by SLOs, the gap to 100% is an error budget to spend on change, and toil is engineered away.

## When to use it
Any service people depend on — scaled down for small teams, never skipped.

Applied in Node at:
- 5.1.3.1 S4 Run smoke check — command `verify-5-1-3-1-s4-run-smoke-check`

- 5.3.4.1 S1 Write hypotheses & abort conditions — command `verify-5-3-4-1-s1-write-hypotheses-and-abort-conditions`

## How to do it
1. Define SLIs from what users experience
2. Set SLOs below 100% and agree an error-budget policy
3. Alert on budget burn, not on causes
4. Respond to incidents with clear command and blameless postmortems
5. Cap toil and plan capacity ahead of demand

## Structure
| Practice | What it gives you |
| --- | --- |
| SLIs & SLOs | A shared, numeric definition of 'reliable enough' |
| Error budgets | A rule for choosing between shipping and fixing |
| Monitoring & alerting | Pages only for user-visible burn |
| Emergency response & postmortems | Fast restore and learning without blame |
| Capacity planning | Demand met with headroom |
| Toil reduction | Time for engineering, not repetition |

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Environment smoke check → `templates/test-environment-record.md`, saved as `docs/test-environment-record.md`

- Fault-injection plan → `templates/resilience-test-report.md`, saved as `docs/resilience-test-report.md`

## Quality checks
- Avoid: Copying Google's tooling instead of its practices
- Avoid: SLOs set at 100%
- Avoid: An 'SRE team' that just does operations
- Environment smoke check: Differences from production listed
- Environment smoke check: Smoke check before use
- Environment smoke check: Owner named
- Load profile: Every result against a QAS measure
- Load profile: Environment differences stated
- Load profile: Raw data linked
- Fault-injection plan: Every fault has a hypothesis and an abort condition
- Fault-injection plan: Runbook steps actually exercised
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

# Stage-gate

_Framework_ — Divides work into stages separated by gates. At each gate a decision-maker reviews the evidence against criteria and decides whether work continues.

## When to use it
For investment decisions that need explicit, auditable checkpoints — in Node, initiative-level decisions. Inside a funded product, the Definition of Ready and Done replace heavy gates.

## How to do it

2. Define gate criteria in advance
3. At the gate, review deliverables against the criteria
4. Decide: Go, Kill, Hold or Recycle — and record why

## Structure
1. Stage: do the work
2. Gate: review evidence
3. Go / Kill / Hold / Recycle
4. Next stage

## Quality checks
- Avoid: Gates that never kill anything
- Avoid: Gates that become bureaucracy without evidence
- Avoid: Gating every feature — use it for investments, agile cadences for the work inside them

# Test pyramid

_Pattern_ — Many fast, cheap tests at the bottom, fewer slower tests above: unit, then service / integration, then a thin layer of end-to-end and UI tests.

Deciding test levels in the strategy.

## Scenarios and measures
_Which QAS, with targets._
> Example: QAS-01: 400 orders/h, 95% ready for review within 60 s.


## Load profile
_Arrival pattern, mix, duration, data._
> Example: Poisson arrivals; 60% clean, 25% poor scans, 15% multi-page; 1 h steady + 8 h soak.


## Environment
_Where, and how it differs from production._
> Example: Staging, half-size; results scaled with the capacity model.

_Per measure: target, observed, pass/fail._
> Example: Load: p95 42 s — pass. Stress at 1,200/h: p95 3.1 min, no errors, degrades gracefully. Soak 8 h: no memory growth.

# Opportunity brief — {initiative}

- **Initiative:** 
- **Owner:** 
- **Version:** 
- **Status: Draft / In review / Approved:** 
- **Last updated:** 

## 1. Problem and users
_The validated problem statement and primary jobs._
> Example: Clerks re-type emailed PDF orders (~2.5 h/day).


## 2. Opportunity and size
_Value range and confidence._
> Example: €375k–€960k/yr; likely €641k; medium confidence.


## 3. Value hypothesis and measure
_What will change and how we'll know._
> Example: Order-handling time 14 → 8 min; error rate 3% → 1%.


## 4. Constraints and key risks
_From the constraint log and risk register._
> Example: ERP import API only; parsing accuracy on poor scans.


## 5. Decision and conditions
_From the decision record._
> Example: Go, conditional on vendor connector by June.

_What the strategy covers and the quality characteristics that matter (ISO/IEC 25010)._
> Example: Order intake service; priorities: functional suitability (accuracy), reliability, security, interaction capability.


## 2. Test levels and ownership
_Pyramid: who owns which level._
> Example: Unit & contract — developers (BUILD); system & E2E — test engineers; UAT — order team leads.

_Functional, performance, security, accessibility, resilience, accuracy evaluation._

_Which environment proves what._
> Example: Preview per pull request; staging is production-like with the ERP test client.


## 5. Test data approach
_Synthetic first; production data only masked and approved._
> Example: 600-PDF corpus; real PDFs anonymised under the DPIA.


## 6. Automation and CI
_What is automated, where it runs, what evidence it records._
> Example: All system cases run in CI against the named build; results carry the run id and link.


## 7. Formality rule
_When formal test cases are required — decided by rule, not habit._
> Example: Formal cases for every Must criterion and every risk rated ≥ 10; charters elsewhere.


## 8. Defects and severities
_Severity scale, triage cadence, what blocks release._
> Example: Sev-1 to Sev-4; no open Sev-1 or Sev-2 at the Quality Gate unless accepted by the risk owner.

files.title: Workflow 5.1.1.1 · Rate Quality Risks
files.body:
# Workflow 5.1.1.1 · Rate Quality Risks

Turn requirements, scenarios, threats and DISCOVER risks into rated quality risks, each with the test depth it earns.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/verify-5-1-1-1-rate-risks.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `verify-5-1-1-1-run-rate-risks`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: verify-5-1-1-1-rate-risks
title: "Rate Quality Risks"
owner: "QA lead"
inputs:
  - "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
  - "docs/qa-scenarios.md"
  - "docs/threat-model.md"
  - "docs/risk-register.md"
preconditions:
  - "Build scope announced"
  - "Test basis baselined"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Collect the test basis"
    owner: "QA lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-1-1-1-s1-collect-the-test-basis
    skills: [istqb-test-process]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer, domain-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Change withdrawn": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Identify quality risks"
    owner: "Product owner, Engineer, Test engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-1-1-1-s2-identify-quality-risks
    skills: [three-amigos, pre-mortem]
    reviewers: [security-reviewer, performance-reviewer, accessibility-reviewer, ai-reviewer, reliability-reviewer, data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/quality-risk-analysis.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Rate likelihood × impact"
    owner: "QA lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-1-1-1-s3-rate-likelihood-impact
    skills: [risk-matrix, risk-based-testing, risk-register]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer]
    output: "docs/quality-risk-analysis.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Product owner agrees?"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Product owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Disputed → re-workshop": s2
      "Beyond PO authority → risk owner": authority
  - id: s4
    do: "Assign test depth & levels"
    owner: "QA lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-1-1-1-s4-assign-test-depth-and-levels
    skills: [impact-analysis, traceability-matrix]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/quality-risk-analysis.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Risk Analysis Agreed"
criteria:
  - "Every Must requirement and QAS mapped"
  - "Every risk has a depth"
checks:
  - "Product owner walk-through"
on_failure:
  - "Cross-check against the risk register and add the gap"
  - "Re-run the rating with the product owner"
rework: "Disputed ratings → re-workshop with evidence"
outputs:
  - "docs/quality-risk-analysis.md"
handoff: "Quality risk analysis → 5.1.2 Define Levels, Types & Exit Criteria"
learning:
  - "Risks that produced defects vs those rated high — learning log"
```

files.title: Subprocess 5.1.1 · Analyse Quality Risks
files.body:
# Subprocess 5.1.1 · Analyse Quality Risks

Spend testing effort where failure would hurt most, decided by evidence rather than habit.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/verify-5-1-1-quality-risks.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `verify-5-1-1-run-quality-risks`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
orchestration: verify-5-1-1-quality-risks
title: "Analyse Quality Risks"
owner: "QA lead"
inputs:
  - "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
  - "docs/vin-criteria.md"
  - "docs/qa-scenarios.md"
  - "docs/threat-model.md"
  - "docs/risk-register.md"
entry:
  - "Build under test announced with its stories"
  - "Requirements baseline, quality-attribute scenarios and threat model available"
runs:
  - unit: "5.1.1.1 Rate Quality Risks"
    spec: workflows/verify-5-1-1-1-rate-risks.md
    command: verify-5-1-1-1-run-rate-risks
    gate: "Risk Analysis Agreed"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
parallel:
  - "Risk identification by quality characteristic runs in parallel with threat review"
gate: "Risk Analysis Agreed"
decided_by: "Product owner agrees ratings; risk owner rules on risks beyond the product owner's authority."
criteria:
  - "Each risk states failure → effect"
  - "Each Must requirement and QAS appears at least once"
  - "Every risk has a test depth"
routes:
  forward: "→ Define Levels, Types & Exit Criteria"
  rework: "Disputed ratings → re-workshop with evidence"
  alternate: "Standing risk list exists → re-rate deltas only"
  escalate: "Impact beyond the product owner's authority → risk owner"
  stop: "Change is withdrawn by BUILD → stop analysis — recorded in the learning log"
outputs:
  - "docs/quality-risk-analysis.md"
handoff: "Quality risk analysis → 5.1.2 Define Levels, Types & Exit Criteria"
```

```yaml

title: "Run the Accessibility Audit"
owner: "Accessibility specialist"
inputs:
  - "docs/qa-scenarios.md"
  - "docs/test-environment-record.md"
preconditions:
  - "Screens deployed in staging"

    do: "Scan screens automatically"
    owner: "Test engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-3-3-1-s1-scan-screens-automatically
    skills: [agile-testing-quadrants]
    reviewers: [accessibility-reviewer]
    output: "docs/accessibility-audit.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Screen out of scope": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Walk through by keyboard"
    owner: "Accessibility specialist"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-3-3-1-s2-walk-through-by-keyboard

    reviewers: [accessibility-reviewer]

  - "Failures a design review could have caught — DESIGN feedback"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 5.4.3.1 · Validate Against the Hypothesis

Measure the outcome the brief promised, baseline against pilot, and conclude whether the right problem is solved.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/verify-5-4-3-1-validate.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `verify-5-4-3-1-run-validate`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: verify-5-4-3-1-validate
title: "Validate Against the Hypothesis"
owner: "Product manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/opportunity-brief.md"
  - "docs/uat-log.md"
preconditions:
  - "Measures and baseline agreed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Restate hypothesis & measures"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-4-3-1-s1-restate-hypothesis-and-measures
    skills: [lean-startup]
    reviewers: [business-reviewer, challenger]
    output: "docs/opportunity-brief.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Measure baseline & pilot like for like"
    owner: "Data analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-4-3-1-s2-measure-baseline-and-pilot-like-for-like
    skills: [time-and-motion-study, site-pilot, feature-flags]
    reviewers: [data-reviewer, domain-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/outcome-validation.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Compare & interpret"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-4-3-1-s3-compare-and-interpret
    skills: [before-after-comparison]
    reviewers: [finance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/outcome-validation.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Right problem solved?"
    owner: "Sponsor"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Sponsor decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Method unreliable → re-measure": s2
      "Far below hypothesis → sponsor": authority
      "Problem not solved → DISCOVER / PLAN": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Record conclusion & signals"
    owner: "Product manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-4-3-1-s4-record-conclusion-and-signals
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/outcome-validation.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Outcome Validated"
criteria:
  - "Like-for-like baseline"
  - "Confidence stated"
checks:
  - "Method review"
on_failure:
  - "Re-measure on replayed real orders"
  - "Rebuild the baseline from the same order mix"
rework: "Unreliable method → re-measure"
outputs:
  - "docs/outcome-validation.md"
handoff: "Outcome validation report → 5.4.4 Obtain Acceptance Sign-off; signals → OPERATE and EVOLVE"
learning:
  - "Predicted vs observed value — EVOLVE"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 5.5.3.1 · Verify a Fix

Fix with a test that would have caught it, ship a new build, re-test there, regress, and only then close.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/verify-5-5-3-1-fix-verify.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `verify-5-5-3-1-run-fix-verify`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: verify-5-5-3-1-fix-verify
title: "Verify a Fix"
owner: "Developers"
inputs:
  - "docs/defect-log.md"
  - "docs/defect-report.md"
preconditions:
  - "Triage decision: fix now"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Fix & add a lowest-level test"
    owner: "Developers"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-5-3-1-s1-fix-and-add-a-lowest-level-test
    skills: [test-pyramid, root-cause-analysis, five-whys]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/test-case.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Fix withdrawn → back to triage": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Deliver a new build"
    owner: "CI pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-5-3-1-s2-deliver-a-new-build
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/vin-build.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Re-test on the new build"
    owner: "Test engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-5-3-1-s3-re-test-on-the-new-build
    skills: [istqb-test-process]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer]
    output: "docs/test-run-evidence.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Run impacted regression"
    owner: "CI pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: verify-5-5-3-1-s4-run-impacted-regression
    skills: [regression-testing, impact-analysis]

  - "docs/defect-log.md"
handoff: "Re-test results & verified defects → Report and Accept Residual Risk (5.5.4)"

  - "Root causes of Sev-1/2 defects — learning log"
```

# Workflow 5.5.4.1 · Report and Accept Residual Risk

State everything known to be wrong or unproven, rate what it leaves, and have an owner with authority accept each risk with conditions and an expiry — or refuse it.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/verify-5-5-4-1-residual-risk.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `verify-5-5-4-1-run-residual-risk`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml

  - "docs/uat-signoff.md"
  - "docs/risk-register.md"
preconditions:
  - "Triage current"
  - "Fix–verify loops closed or decided"
steps:
  - id: s1

    owner: "QA lead"

    branches:
      "yes": s3

      "Mitigation unverified → verify first": s1
  - id: s3
    do: "Owner accepts with conditions & expiry"
    owner: "Risk owner"

    command: verify-5-5-4-1-s3-owner-accepts-with-conditions-and-expiry

  - "docs/risk-acceptance.md"

  - "Accepted risks that materialised in OPERATE — learning log"
```

# Workflow 5.5.4.2 · Hold the Quality Gate

```yaml

  - "docs/nft-summary.md"
  - "docs/uat-signoff.md"

  - "docs/defect-report.md"

steps:

    owner: "QA lead"

  - "Gate outcomes vs production escapes — learning log"
```

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act V VERIFY · Scale: Product team. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
VERIFY is part of the **Delivery track** — Are we building the thing right? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## VERIFY: Demonstrate with evidence that the increment works as specified, meets its quality attributes and solves the right problem — at a risk someone has knowingly accepted.
- **5.1 Test Strategy & Planning** — gate: Test Plan Approved. Produces: Quality risk analysis, Test strategy, Release test plan, Test environment record, Test data plan.
- **5.2 Functional Verification** — gate: Verification Signed. Produces: Test cases traced to criteria, Traceability matrix, Test-run evidence, Exploratory session sheet, Regression suite, Verification sign-off.
- **5.3 Non-Functional Verification** — gate: NFR Verification. Produces: Performance test report, Security test report, Accessibility audit report, Resilience test report, Non-functional results, Extraction accuracy evaluation.
- **5.4 Acceptance & Validation** — gate: Acceptance Sign-off. Produces: UAT plan, UAT execution log, Outcome validation report, UAT sign-off.
- **5.5 Defect Triage & Resolution** — gate: Quality Gate. Produces: Defect log, Defect & residual-risk report, Risk acceptances, Quality gate record, Verification retrospective, Learning log.
- Act gate: **Quality Gate** — decided by: QA lead decides the gate with the product owner; the business acceptor signs UAT; the risk owner accepts residual risk; the sponsor rules above appetite..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: STY → TST → TC → TR → NFT → UAT → DEF → RRA → QGR → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `verify-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Product team
Write for a product trio and a delivery team. Use our shared templates, make outputs ready to drop into the backlog or repository, and flag anything that needs the team's refinement.
Access: Read and write the shared workspace and backlog; agents propose changes, people merge and publish.
